newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEKS IN HIGH-INCOME TAX BRACKETS SHOULD INVEST ABROAD - STUDY.
newsitem.headline: GREEKS IN HIGH-INCOME TAX BRACKETS SHOULD INVEST ABROAD - STUDY.

text.p: Greece's tax system pushes high-income tax bracket investors subject to a marginal tax rate greater than 30 percent to favour foreign stocks and interest income, said a study on the taxation of Greek bonds and stocks.

"Investors with marginal tax rates greater than about 30 percent, should benefit by investing in foreign stocks through institutional investors," said a study authored by National Bank of Greece deputy governor Nick Karamouzis and researcher Dimitris Georgoutsos.
"The same conclusion holds for interest income," said the study.
The study, titled 'The Taxation of Securities in Greece' looks into the tax burden of income from stocks and bonds.
It appears in a book on the functioning of Greece's public sector published by the private Foundation of Economic and Industrial Research (IOBE).
Individuals at low income tax brackets should benefit by investing in securities that pay interest instead of dividends, the study said.
Small shareholders were hurt by the abolition of the tax-exempt limit on dividend income in 1992, the study said.

Greece's tax system does not discriminate between investing directly or through institutions in domestic equities as far as dividend income is concerned but favours the direct purchase of stocks on the basis of income from capital gains, the study said.

"In general, portfolio income from domestic stocks and bonds have a lower tax burden than that coming from foreign stocks and bonds. The reason is that no credit is given for taxes paid at the corporate level," it said.
"So the capital export neutrality principle does not hold for this type of income," it added. "Under certain conditions, it holds for intra-company (monther-subsidiary) cash flows."
The tax burden is lower in countries such as France and Germany that have adopted the imputation system than others such as the U.S. with the classic taxation system.
In the U.S. coprorate profits are subject to double taxation at the corporate level as well as at the individual's marginal tax rate.
